azure-database-mysql-01000.description:
To migrate a Java application that uses a MySQL database to Azure, you can follow these recommendations:

 * Use a managed **Azure Database for MySQL**: For that create a managed MySQL database in Azure and choose the appropriate pricing tier based on your application's requirements for performance, storage, and availability.

 * **Migrate** the existing MySQL database: For that you can use the Azure Database Migration Service (DMS) to perform an online migration with minimal downtime.

 * Update the application's **database connection** details: Modify the Java application's configuration to point to the newly provisioned Azure Database for MySQL. Update the connection string, hostname, port, username, and password information accordingly.

 * Enable **monitoring and diagnostics**: Utilize Azure Monitor to gain insights into the performance and health of your Java application and the underlying MySQL database. Set up metrics, alerts, and log analytics to proactively identify and resolve issues.

 * Implement **security** measures: Apply security best practices to protect your Java application and the MySQL database. This includes implementing authentication and authorization mechanisms with passwordless connections and leveraging Microsoft Defender for Cloud for threat detection and vulnerability assessments.

 * **Backup** your data: Azure Database for MySQL provides automated backups by default. You can configure the retention period for backups based on your requirements. You can also enable geo-redundant backups, if needed, to enhance data durability and availability.
azure-database-mysql-01000.title: MySQL database found

links.title: Backup and restore in Azure Database for MySQL

Upgrading to the latest LTS version ensures your application benefits from the most recent security enhancements and a longer support lifecycle.

cra-insecure-tls-trust-all-03000.description:
**EU Cyber Resilience Act (Annex I, Part I, Section 2(c)(d))** requires that data confidentiality and integrity are protected during transit using state of the art mechanisms.

Implementing a custom `X509TrustManager` that does not properly validate certificates (trust-all pattern) completely disables TLS certificate verification. This makes the application vulnerable to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.

**Recommended actions:**
* Remove custom `TrustManager` implementations that accept all certificates.
* Use the default `TrustManagerFactory` with the system or a properly configured trust store.
* If you need custom certificate handling, use certificate pinning instead.
* For development/testing, use profiles or environment-specific configurations instead of disabling validation in code.
cra-insecure-tls-trust-all-03000.title: CRA: Certificate validation bypass - TrustAllCerts

dockerfile-00000.description:
No Dockerfile was found in the project. This suggests the application may not yet be containerized. 
Consider creating a Dockerfile to enable container-based replatforming to Azure services such as Azure Container Apps or AKS.
dockerfile-00000.title: No Dockerfile found

hardcoded-urls-00001.description: This patterns verifies in source code and configuration files the presence of hardcoded URLs using the HTTP protocol (HTTP/HTTPS). This URL would need to be replaced by the new resource's URL during the Cloud migration, if any change occured.
hardcoded-urls-00001.title: Avoid using hardcoded URLs (HTTP protocol) in source code

logging-0002.description:
Detected a logging configuration that writes logs to the local file system. In Azure environments, file-based appenders are discouraged due to ephemeral storage and lack of centralized access.

Recommendations:
* Switch to console appenders only (Logback / Log4j) and disable file or rolling file appenders.
* Collect logs using Azure Monitor Logs (workspace-based Application Insights) via diagnostic settings.
* Output structured JSON logs to improve KQL querying and cross-service correlation.
logging-0002.title: Avoid File System Logging in Configuration

links.title: Enable diagnostics logging for apps in Azure App Service

quartz-scheduler-to-azure-functions-0100.description:
The application uses Quartz Scheduler for scheduled jobs. Consider migrating scheduled workloads to Azure Functions using a Timer trigger.
Azure Functions Timer Trigger supports NCRONTAB (cron-like) schedules and can replace many Quartz scheduling use cases while reducing infrastructure management overhead.
You will need to replace Quartz jobs/triggers (and any persistent job store configuration) with timer-triggered Azure Functions, and move any state/persistence to external services (for example, Azure Storage, databases, or queues) as appropriate.
quartz-scheduler-to-azure-functions-0100.title: Quartz Scheduler usage detected

sqlite-to-azure-postgresql-01000.description:
The application uses SQLite. Consider migrating to Azure Database for PostgreSQL.
Azure Database for PostgreSQL provides a fully managed, multi-user PostgreSQL service with advanced SQL features and scalability beyond single-file databases.
You will need to replace the SQLite JDBC driver and connection configuration, review SQL and schema differences (for example, data types, AUTOINCREMENT/sequence behavior, and concurrency/locking semantics), and perform schema/data migration from SQLite files to PostgreSQL.
sqlite-to-azure-postgresql-01000.title: SQLite usage detected

links.title: What is Azure Database for PostgreSQL?
Use Azure (SDK) libraries in Java to create, update, and delete an Azure Database for PostgreSQL

unsecure-network-protocol-00000.description:
Using secured protocols such as HTTPS and SFTP (over HTTP and FTP) should now be the norm as applications are more and more exposed and interconnected. 
This CloudReady patterns looks for unescured URI in the source code or deprecated URI libraries. 
Ideally, URLs should be replaced in your source code by secured protocols HTTPS and SFTP (and ensure the infrastructure implements these protocols for the resources your application calls, uses or references).
unsecure-network-protocol-00000.title: Use of unsecured network protocols or URI libraries

security.title: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
security.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

evidence.explanation: In ImportByWxMp.java at lines 262 and 345, wxMpUserList.getTotal() returns a long value that is cast to int via (int) without bounds checking. If the total number of WeChat subscribers exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647), the cast truncates the value, causing the progress bar maximum to be set incorrectly and potentially causing UI logic errors.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: In HikariUtil.java, the executeQuery() method (lines 61-63) creates a database Connection and PreparedStatement but returns the ResultSet to the caller without closing them. The caller receives only the ResultSet and has no way to close the underlying Connection and PreparedStatement, leading to connection pool resource exhaustion over time.

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: In TaskHisDetailDialog.java (lines 148, 216, 284), DataInputStream is created wrapping a FileInputStream, then passed to CSVReader via InputStreamReader. Only the outer CSVReader (reader) is closed in the finally block. If the CSVReader or InputStreamReader constructor fails, the DataInputStream and FileInputStream are never closed, leaving file descriptors open.

security.title: Data Access Operations Outside of Expected Data Manager Component
security.description: The product uses a dedicated, central data manager component as required by design, but it contains code that performs data-access operations that do not use this data manager.

evidence.explanation: In TaskForm.java (lines 77-82), UI form classes directly instantiate and use MyBatis mapper objects (TTaskMapper, TPeopleMapper, TMsgMapper, etc.) obtained via MybatisUtil.getSqlSession().getMapper() to perform database operations. Data access is scattered across UI layer classes (TaskForm, PeopleEditForm, etc.) instead of being centralized in a dedicated data manager or service layer, violating separation of concerns.

security.title: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

evidence.explanation: In TaskForm.java (lines 88-92), the getInstance() method checks 'if (taskForm == null)' and creates a new instance without any synchronization. The same unsynchronized singleton pattern exists in PeopleEditForm.java, MessageEditForm.java, and several other form classes. TaskRunThread.java calls TaskForm.getInstance() from a background thread (lines 284, 337, 395), creating a race condition where the singleton instance could be created multiple times or accessed in an inconsistent state.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: In MessageManageForm.java at line 50, the public static boolean 'accountSwitchComboBoxListenIgnore' is a shared mutable static field that is read and written from both the Swing EDT and background task threads without synchronization. Additionally, the static 'accountMap' field (line 44) is a Map shared across threads without any synchronization guard, potentially leading to ConcurrentModificationException or stale reads.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: In TaskForm.java, the static singleton field 'taskForm' and mapper fields (taskMapper, taskHisMapper, peopleMapper, msgMapper at lines 77-82) are shared static resources accessed from both the Swing EDT and background TaskRunThread instances without any synchronization. The MyBatis SqlSession obtained via MybatisUtil.getSqlSession() is a single shared non-thread-safe session used concurrently from multiple threads through these static mapper references.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The application has 44 occurrences of e.printStackTrace() across the codebase (e.g., ImportByFile.java lines 293, 307) instead of using the structured logger (log.error()). Security-critical failures such as file access errors, database connection failures, and message send failures are silently swallowed with only a console stack trace rather than being recorded in the application's security log. This makes post-incident analysis and security auditing difficult.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: In ImportByFile.java, the method importFromFile (line 127) accepts a filePath parameter obtained directly from user input (memberFilePathField.getText() at line 110) and passes it to new File(filePath) at line 136 without any canonicalization or path restriction check. A user can type an arbitrary path (e.g., ../../../etc/passwd) and the application will attempt to open it, bypassing any intended directory restriction.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: In ImportByFile.java at line 110-136, the filePath is taken from memberFilePathField.getText() and passed to new File(filePath) without neutralizing relative sequences such as '../'. An attacker could supply a path like '../../sensitive/file.csv' to read files outside any intended directory.

security.title: Absolute Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: In ImportByFile.java at line 110-136, the user-supplied filePath (from memberFilePathField.getText()) is used directly in new File(filePath) without restricting or validating absolute paths. A user can type an absolute path such as '/etc/passwd' or 'C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM' to access sensitive files outside any intended directory.

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.

evidence.explanation: In HttpMsgSender.java (lines 87-229), the URL for HTTP requests is taken directly from user-configured message data (httpMsg.getUrl()) without restriction or validation. The URL is passed directly to HttpRequest.get/post/put/delete/patch/head/options and OkHttp's urlBuilder, allowing requests to arbitrary internal or external resources including internal services (SSRF).

security.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
security.description: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.

evidence.explanation: In UpgradeUtil.java at lines 36 and 45, remote JSON content is fetched via HTTP from a GitHub URL (UiConsts.CHECK_VERSION_URL) and immediately deserialized using fastjson 1.2.74 (JSON.parseObject). Fastjson 1.2.74 is affected by CVE-2022-25845 (unsafe deserialization), meaning that a compromised or man-in-the-middle server response containing a malicious '@type' field could trigger arbitrary code execution during deserialization.

security.title: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
security.description: The product uses, accesses, or otherwise operates on a resource after that resource has been expired, released, or revoked.

evidence.explanation: In HikariUtil.java, the executeQuery() method (lines 61-63) opens a database connection and PreparedStatement but returns the ResultSet without closing the PreparedStatement or Connection. Callers that use the ResultSet cannot properly close the underlying Connection, causing connection pool resources to be held open after the ResultSet is consumed. This constitutes operating on a resource (connection pool slot) after the intended use scope has ended.
